page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual machine utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It provides two vCPUs derived from a single dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 physical core operating two threads. The configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, with 32 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached disks for persistent data, and does not include hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-standard-2 exhibits strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a stress-ng single-core score of 2923.48, placing it in the top quartile. However, overall multi-core and system-wide throughput reflect its small hardware footprint. The multi-core stress-ng score reaches 2928.18, and Geekbench multi-core registers at 2021.0, both falling into lower percentiles due to the two-vCPU ceiling. Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate 33.76 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 24.26 GB/sec for writes. Application benchmarks show average performance in single-threaded tasks like gzip compression at 27.81 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 11.99 GB/sec, while database operations, Clang compilation, and Redis SET throughput (2.22 million operations per second) are restrained by total core capacity.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the c2d-standard-2 provides a cost-efficient entry point to dedicated AMD EPYC compute without paying for oversized thread counts. The primary tradeoff lies in the aggregate parallel capacity and memory subsystem speeds, making it unsuitable for heavy compilation pipelines, large in-memory databases, or multi-threaded batch jobs. It is best configured for lightweight compute tasks, small worker microservices, single-threaded processing queues, static web serving, and entry-level small-model LLM text generation.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is a compute-optimized instance based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supplying two vCPUs across one dedicated physical core with two threads. The machine is paired with 8.0 GB of RAM, offering 4.0 GB of memory per core alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. It excludes attached local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on remote persistent disks for storage needs. In performance testing, c2d-standard-2 delivers strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng benchmarks, complemented by average single-threaded compression and small-scale LLM text generation throughput. Aggregate multi-core throughput, compilation speed, and memory bandwidth reflect its small dual-thread footprint. The instance represents a cost-efficient hardware choice for compute-focused services that do not require high concurrency, making it appropriate for lightweight worker processes, single-threaded ETL tasks, static web serving, and basic microservices.
